context: A police officer briefs a uni reporter about administrative reform
purpose: Teach: 原案/本業/都度/縛ら/検事/集客/文言/網羅

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: 本業の警備に加え、集客イベントの安全管理も担当しています。
lines.en: In addition to core security work, we also manage safety for customer events and promotional activities.
lines.style: Even, measured opening. Professional clarity without stiffness. Steady eye contact level. Informational but not lecturing—the tone of someone used to explaining their role.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 原案づくり、検事と協議されるんですか。
lines.en: When you're drafting those plans, do you coordinate with prosecutors?
lines.style: Genuine curiosity, slight lean forward. Not defensive—testing to understand. Respectful pause before the question, as if he's thought about whether to ask it.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: はい、都度確認しています。文言の網羅性が重要です。
lines.en: Yes—we confirm each time. The comprehensiveness of the wording is crucial.
lines.style: Direct acknowledgement on 「はい」. Shift to technical register. Slight emphasis on 「網羅性」 without sounding pedantic. Clinical but not cold.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 過去の事案に縛られず、柔軟に対応していらっしゃるんですね。
lines.en: So you don't get locked into past precedents—you stay flexible with how you approach each situation.
lines.style: Warm recognition in the voice. Small smile underneath the words. Genuinely impressed, not flattering. Slower pace on the observation, giving him room to hear himself reflected back.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: はい。それが安全につながります。
lines.en: Yes. That's what leads to real safety.
lines.style: Quiet conviction. Not defensive—affirming. Brief, weighted pause before the final word. The quiet confidence of someone who's seen how flexibility saves lives.
